name: Toad
desc: The warty brown hopper that squats in the damp garden, fatter and drier than a frog.
prose: You are a toad - the warty brown squatter of the damp garden, fatter and drier and slower than your cousin the frog. You hide all day under a cool stone and come out at dusk to snap up slugs and beetles with a flick of your tongue. Your skin is bumpy and your eyes are gold, and a fairy tale swears a kiss will turn you to a prince. You do not leap so much as lumber. You are the gardener's quiet friend, ugly and useful, lurking in the cool dark with a stomach full of pests.

lines: A little bug that glows in the dark,
it blinks across the summer lawn -
A soft light thing that grows on a bird,
it drifts down on the air;
you tickle a nose or stuff a pillow -
A little lizard that swims in the pond,
with a wavy crest on its back;
it wriggles through the weedy dark -
A round-eyed bird that hunts at night,
it hoots from a hollow tree;
it swoops on mice with silent wings -
an ___, as wise as can be.
